issues.t: Head gasket leaks oil and coolant
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the joint between the engine block and cylinder head, coolant loss, overheating, or white exhaust smoke. Often around 60,000–70,000 miles.
issues.why: The head gasket on the first-generation Neon 2.0L deteriorates early and starts leaking oil and coolant.
issues.next: Watch the oil and coolant levels and the temperature gauge. Have a leak and cooling system test done, and replace the gasket before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Radiator failure mixes coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Overheating, pink or foamy fluid in the radiator, then slipping, rough shifting or no reverse from the automatic.
issues.why: The automatic transmission cooler is built into the radiator. When the radiator cracks inside or the cooler fitting strips, coolant and transmission fluid mix, which ruins the transmission.
issues.next: Stop driving if you see pink foamy coolant or the transmission starts slipping. Replace the radiator and flush the transmission several times right away; waiting usually means a new transmission.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: The car suddenly acts as if it is in neutral, slips, will not go into gear, or makes clunking or whining noises.
issues.why: The automatic transmission in this generation wears out, and many failures follow coolant contaminating the fluid through a leaking cooler in the radiator.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and color. Have the cooler and radiator checked too, so a new transmission does not fail the same way.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan does not turn on
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs in traffic or at idle but drops when moving at speed. The fan does not run when the engine is hot.
issues.why: The electric radiator fan motor, its relay or its wiring fails. RepairPal lists this as the most common Neon problem.
issues.next: Watch the gauge and avoid idling when hot. Have the fan, relay and fuse tested before the engine overheats and damages the head gasket.

issues.t: Spark plug tube seals leak oil and cause misfires
issues.sym: Misfires, a rough idle, a check engine light and poor fuel economy. Oil is found on the spark plugs or in the plug wells.
issues.why: The seals around the spark plug tubes in the valve cover fail and let engine oil fill the tubes and soak the plugs.
issues.next: Have the plug wells checked for oil. Replacing the seals (usually with the valve cover gasket) and the oily plugs and wires fixes it.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges fail
issues.sym: The speedometer jumps around or quits, gauges go dead or point the wrong way, or the whole dash goes dark while driving.
issues.why: The instrument cluster or its wiring and fuse fail. Owners report it gets worse in wet or humid weather.
issues.next: Check the related fuses first. If the cluster is at fault, a rebuilt cluster is an option besides a new one.

issues.t: Engine mounts fail
issues.sym: Heavy vibration, a clunk when shifting into gear or accelerating, and the engine rocking.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts break down. Some owners needed them again within a year.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Broken mounts strain hoses, wiring and axles.

issues.t: Misfires and stalling from cam or crank sensor faults
issues.sym: A check engine light with codes P0335, P0340 or P0301, rough idle, misfires, stalling at stops, or loss of power.
issues.why: Owners trace it to failed camshaft or crankshaft position sensors or their wiring, and to worn plugs, wires and coils.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Check the sensor wiring for damage before replacing sensors again, and replace old plugs and wires.

issues.t: Engine will not start
issues.sym: No crank or no start even though the lights and radio work, or the engine starts but will not stay running.
issues.why: Causes reported include a weak battery or starter and, in one case, a corroded engine computer whose seal had failed.
issues.next: Test the battery and starter first. If they are good, have the engine computer and its connectors checked for corrosion.

issues.t: Paint peeling
issues.sym: Paint and clear coat flaking off, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.why: The factory paint loses its bond to the layer underneath.
issues.next: Cosmetic only. Get repaint quotes for the worst panels and keep bare metal covered to stop rust.

issues.t: Noisy brake pads
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the brakes.
issues.why: Owners report noisy front pads that needed replacing early.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors checked; grinding means metal on metal and needs attention right away.

issues.t: Horn stops working
issues.sym: The horn does not sound when the pad is pressed.
issues.why: Owners report the horn failing; common causes are the horn switch, clockspring in the steering wheel, relay or the horn itself.
issues.next: Have the fuse and relay checked first, then the horn and steering wheel wiring.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum hose can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal and a higher than normal idle speed.
issues.why: The vacuum hose to the brake booster can fail, causing loss of power brake assist. Recall 01V-154.
issues.next: If the pedal suddenly feels hard, brake earlier and harder and get it checked. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Throttle can ice up and stick (recall)
issues.sym: In cold, damp weather the engine does not return fully to idle when you lift off the gas.
issues.why: Ice can form on the throttle blade and hold it partly open. Recall 00V-194.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the idle stays high, shift to neutral and brake.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; a child seat may not be properly anchored.
issues.why: The child seat tether anchors did not meet the federal standard. Recall 00V-366.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall before installing a child seat.

issues.t: Lower control arm weld can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension or the car pulling and wandering.
issues.why: Poor welding on some lower control arms could let the arm come apart. Recall 99V-114 covered a small number of cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the front suspension inspected if it clunks.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on and the pedal goes lower or feels soft.
issues.why: The master cylinder can leak fluid, cutting braking on half of the split system. Recall 96V-075.
issues.next: Do not ignore the brake light. Check fluid level and have the brakes inspected; check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Under-hood wiring can short and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Electrical problems and the engine stalling.
issues.why: The front under-hood wiring harness can short out. Recall 96V-026.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have any electrical faults diagnosed.

issues.t: Body spot welds may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Cracks in the body structure, creaks, or no symptom at all.
issues.why: Some cars were built with defective spot welds, which can crack the body and weaken rear crash protection. Recall 99V-001.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Water leaks into the trunk and back seat
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the trunk or behind the rear seat, a musty smell or mold, and sometimes water dripping in from the top of a door after rain.
issues.why: Water gets past aging door and trunk seals or gaps in the body seams around the trunk. Owners report the leaks coming back over time.
issues.next: Dry the carpet quickly to stop mold and rust. A body shop can find the entry point with a water or smoke test, then replace the seal or reseal the seam.
